Hi Marissa,

Thank you for the draft order form and security exhibit. We ran this by procurement and security here at Sanford and have a few items we'd like to align on before we sign. High-level asks:
- Clarify pen-test notice window and whether Redwood will accept a 48-hour staging-only window for live tests.
- SOC 2: can we confirm the list of covered systems and the reporting cadence for SOC 2 changes? We typically ask for annual attestations and a notice if controls materially change.
- Audit rights: we need an evidence cadence that doesn't require on-demand access to production — a scheduled evidence bundle and a maximum of two inspections per year is our baseline.

Attached: a short checklist the security team filled out (we'll share formally if needed).

Can you propose a concrete cadence and any contract language you'd prefer for the Order Form / Security Exhibit? If we can get a proposed response by Thursday we can move to legal review on our side.

Thanks,
Emma

Emma — thanks for the clear list. We appreciate Sanford's constraints. Proposed summary below and attached a redline of the Security Exhibit (Redwood_Security_Exhibit_v3.docx) and a pen-test window proposal spreadsheet. TL;DR: we can accommodate a scheduled evidence bundle and two inspections per year with a defined playbook, and we can offer a 48-hour staging-only pen-test window with a short ops checklist.

Proposed items (high level):
1) Evidence cadence: quarterly scheduled evidence bundles (SOC 2 report + scoped artifacts) delivered via secure link, with one additional ad hoc evidence request per year limited to non-production artifacts unless otherwise negotiated.
2) Audit rights: explicit language that says scheduled inspections (max 2 per calendar year) are permitted; ad hoc inspections require 30 days' notice and written justification, and Redwood reserves the right to require a scoped assessment or remote evidence in lieu of live production access.
3) SOC 2: annual SOC 2 Type II report included; Redwood will notify Sanford within 10 business days if control scope materially changes.
4) Pen test windows: 48-hour staging-only window acceptable; live production tests require 14 days' advanced coordination and written ops runbook. Third-party testers must be named and have signed NDAs; Redwood will provide a point of contact for the window.

As requested, attachments: Redwood_Security_Exhibit_v3.docx (redline), PenTest_Window_Proposal.xlsx, OrderForm_Sanford_v2.pdf (order form draft).

Next steps: Karthik and Laura from Legal will propose final wording for the audit-rights and SOC clauses; can we schedule a 30-minute call Thursday at 10am PT to walk through the redline? If that time works, I'll send a calendar invite.

Best,
Marissa Cole

Emma / Marissa — looping in legal language suggestions and a suggested non-production-first clause. I captured the edits inline in the attached v3 docx but summarizing here so procurement has something to review quickly: 

- Audit rights (proposed clause): 
"Customer may conduct up to two on-site inspections per calendar year or request remote evidence reviews. Any additional inspections will require 30 days' prior written notice and are limited to scoped artifacts. Redwood will not be required to provide unfettered or real-time access to production systems; instead, Redwood will provide scheduled evidence bundles and cooperate with agreed-upon inspection playbooks."

- SOC 2 notifications: add a 10-business-day notice obligation when Redwood becomes aware of any material change to control scope or an adverse SOC 2 finding that affects Sanford's data.

- Pen testing: require testers to be approved in writing; Redwood can require tests to run in a staging environment by default. For live environment tests we propose a 14-day scheduling requirement and an incident escalation plan with named contacts.

- Remedy of findings: propose a 45-day remediation SLA for low/medium findings and a 7-business-day initial response for high/critical findings, with status updates every 5 business days until resolved.

Note on evidence cadence: Legal prefers quarterly scheduled bundles + one ad hoc request allowed per year for non-production artifacts. If Sanford needs more frequent evidence, we can propose an uplift (professional services time) to support additional evidence pulls.

If that summary looks ok Emma, Laura and I can convert this to clean contract language for the Order Form and Security Exhibit. Marissa — please go ahead and book the Thursday slot; I'll be on the call and prepared to walk Laura through the edits.

Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
Attachment: Redwood_Security_Exhibit_v3.docx (redlines included)

Thanks Karthik, Marissa — that all looks reasonable and close to what our security/compliance team will accept. A few quick clarifications from procurement/security: 
- The scheduled evidence bundles are fine, but please include a short index file (CSV) with artifact names and dates so our automated intake can ingest.
- For pen-tests, Sanford will name the third-party tester in advance; we appreciate Redwood's staging-first preference and will expect the 14-day notice for any live testing.
- The remediation SLAs are acceptable. For high/critical items we may request a call within 24 hours for immediate triage; would Redwood commit to that escalation step?

If you can include the index-file requirement and the 24-hour high/critical triage call in the next redline, we can finalize on our side. Let's take the Thursday call to confirm language and sign-off.

I'll sign the calendar invite once Marissa proposes the time.

Best,
